story_title: Iowa's Energy Transition: From Fossil Fuels to Renewables
story_subtitle: Analyzing the shift in electricity generation sources from 2001 to 2017

story_pieces.narration: Fossil Fuels dominated Iowa's electricity generation from 2001 to 2017, peaking at 42,734 GWh in 2007 before declining to 28,437 GWh in 2016.
story_pieces.question: What was the peak year for fossil fuel generation and how did it decline over time?
story_pieces.visualization: line chart (years vs. net generation for Fossil Fuels)

story_pieces.narration: Nuclear Energy production fluctuated between 3,853 GWh and 5,321 GWh, with two distinct peaks in 2008 and 2013.
story_pieces.question: Which years saw the highest nuclear energy production and what patterns emerged?
story_pieces.visualization: bar chart (years vs. net generation for Nuclear Energy)

story_pieces.narration: Renewables experienced exponential growth from 1,437 GWh in 2001 to 21,933 GWh in 2017, outpacing both fossil fuels and nuclear energy.
story_pieces.question: How did renewable energy generation grow compared to other sources over the 17-year period?
story_pieces.visualization: line chart (years vs. net generation for Renewables)

story_pieces.narration: Fossil Fuels accounted for over 80% of total generation in 2001, but their share dropped to 51.93% by 2017 as renewables grew.
story_pieces.question: How has the market share of fossil fuels changed compared to renewables over time?
story_pieces.visualization: stacked area chart (years vs. generation by source)

story_pieces.narration: The generation gap between fossil fuels and renewables widened significantly, with renewables approaching fossil fuels in 2017.
story_pieces.question: When did renewables overtake fossil fuels in generation capacity and what trends define this shift?
story_pieces.visualization: bar chart race (years vs. generation by source)
